source_name: ČNB – Seznam schválených a notifikovaných prospektů
why_relevant: Register of approved and notified prospectuses (plus a companion register of final terms of base prospectuses). Reveals which regulated CZ issuers – including banks and fintech issuers – are raising funds and under what supervisory approvals.

source_name: ČNB MiCA / CASP licensing news and register entries
source_subtype: regulator news + licensing statistics feeding a register
why_relevant: New register population under MiCA: transitional period ended 1.7.2026, ČNB processed 251 applications and granted 11 CASP licences; holders are published in the regulated-entity lists once the decision is final. Announcements give counts and dates before the register reflects them – a leading indicator plus a hard deadline for our deadlines topic.

source_name: ESMA registers and databases (incl. MiCA CASP register)
why_relevant: Linked from ČNB's own Ostatní seznamy page as the EU-level register layer. Contains the consolidated MiCA CASP register and other EU registers where CZ-authorised entities and passporting firms appear – lets us see CZ entities operating cross-border and foreign entities passporting into CZ.

source_name: EBA supervisory disclosure / registers (linked by ČNB)
why_relevant: ČNB links EBA supervisory disclosure as an official complement to its own lists (e.g. the ECAI list under CRR). The EBA also hosts the central PSD2 payment-institution register aggregating national registers, which lets us validate ČNB payments-register content against the EU aggregate.

source_name: ČNB – Informace poskytnuté podle zákona č. 106/1999 Sb. (FOI responses)
why_relevant: FOI answers frequently release register-derived statistics that are not otherwise published (e.g. counts and breakdowns of financial advisers and intermediaries). Also a lever: we can file our own 106/1999 request for register extracts the public UI does not expose.

source_name: Pravniprostor.cz / finreg.cz – Czech legal commentary tracking ČNB supervisory and licensing activity
why_relevant: Czech financial-regulation law blogs summarise ČNB supervisory statistics (inspection counts, DORA first inspections, crypto-licence application volumes) and decode enforcement decisions faster than the primary register. Useful as an interpretation layer and as an early pointer to decisions worth pulling from ABOK.

source_name: Ministerstvo financí ČR — Finanční trh: Bankovnictví a dohled (odbor Finanční trhy)
why_relevant: MF ČR is the statute-level author for banking and payments law in CZ. This section hosts právní rámce, aktuality and consultation announcements for the banking/supervision agenda before anything reaches ČNB implementation.

source_name: MF ČR — Platební služby a vypořádání obchodů (aktuality / konzultace)
why_relevant: The single most on-point MF page for zákon o platebním styku (370/2017 Sb.) amendments, PSD/PSR-related adaptation drafts and public consultations. Historic pattern shows consultation notices posted here with comment deadlines and a contact mailbox.

source_name: MF ČR — Tiskové zprávy (press releases)
why_relevant: Fastest-signalling MF channel: announces government approval of bills, submission to the Chamber of Deputies, and policy intent, usually the same day. Good early-warning trigger for deeper eKLEP/PSP lookups.

source_name: MF ČR — Zpravodaj MF (monthly ministry bulletin)
why_relevant: Monthly consolidated digest of MF activity including legislative work; useful as a low-noise backstop that catches items missed between crawls.

source_name: MF ČR — Zpráva o vývoji finančního trhu (annual financial market report)
why_relevant: Annual MF report includes a dedicated chapter on national and EU legislative activity in the financial market — an authoritative retrospective index of what changed and what is pending; useful for backfilling a legislative timeline.

source_name: Vláda ČR — Plán legislativních prací vlády / Výhled legislativních prací
why_relevant: Government's own forward calendar of legislative tasks, naming the responsible ministry and the target month of submission. Gives 6-24 months of advance visibility on planned banking/payments statutes and EU transposition obligations.

source_name: Vláda ČR — Výsledky jednání vlády / program schůze vlády
why_relevant: Per-meeting record of which bills the government approved and with what modifications — the gate between the comment procedure and Parliament. Dated, hard evidence of a bill advancing.

source_name: Poslanecká sněmovna PČR — Sněmovní tisky (bill database + historie tisku)
why_relevant: Authoritative parliamentary tracking: every bill gets a tisk number with full document set (návrh, důvodová zpráva, pozměňovací návrhy, stanovisko vlády) and a dated stage-by-stage 'historie' page. This is where reading dates, committee referrals and votes become predictable.

source_name: Poslanecká sněmovna — schůze, pořad a stav projednávání (session agendas)
why_relevant: Shows the agenda of each plenary sitting and the live processing state of each item — the practical way to anticipate when a payments/banking bill will actually be debated.

source_name: Senát PČR — senátní tisky, legislativní proces a historie tisku
why_relevant: Second chamber stage: covers the 30-day window where a financial-market bill can be returned with amendments or vetoed, plus committee opinions. Necessary to date účinnost accurately.

source_name: e-Sbírka — Sbírka zákonů a mezinárodních smluv (Ministerstvo vnitra)
why_relevant: Legally binding electronic collection of laws since 1 Jan 2024; gives the final promulgated text, the částka number, and — critically — the účinnost (entry-into-force) dates of banking/payments amendments, with consolidated versions.

source_name: ISAP — Informační systém pro aproximaci práva (Úřad vlády)
why_relevant: Government database tracking EU acts from adoption through Czech implementation, including transposition deadlines, compatibility assessments and which national bill implements which directive. Directly answers 'how and when will PSD3/PSR/other EU payment acts land in CZ law'.

source_name: Hospodářská komora ČR — Připomínkované legislativní materiály
why_relevant: HK ČR is a mandatory comment body and republishes each material entering the comment procedure with its own numbering (e.g. 66/25) and an explicit deadline 'T:dd.mm.yyyy'. Far easier to monitor than eKLEP itself and it surfaces business-side objections.

source_name: MF ČR — Ochrana spotřebitele / spotřebitelské úvěry aktuality (comment-procedure notices)
why_relevant: Adjacent MF workstream that repeatedly announces meziresortní připomínkové řízení for consumer-credit and distance-financial-services bills, which routinely also amend the payments and banking acts.

source_name: MF ČR — Kapitálový trh: konzultace a připomínková řízení
why_relevant: Same MF legislative machinery for the capital-market leg of 'sector=both'; consultation notices here carry named contact mailboxes and explicit comment deadlines, and the omnibus 'změna některých zákonů v oblasti finančního trhu' bills usually touch banking too.

source_name: MF ČR — archiv veřejných konzultací (veřejné diskuze)
why_relevant: Historic archive of numbered MF public consultations (e.g. 'Veřejná konzultace č. V/2012' on the payments act) — useful for reconstructing how MF consults, typical lead times, and which stakeholders respond.

source_name: Právní prostor / Czech law-firm legislative commentary (pravniprostor.cz, konecna-zacha.com, arws.cz, danovky.cz)
why_relevant: Practitioner commentary explains what an MF draft actually changes and flags business impact quickly, often within days of the comment procedure opening. Useful for interpretation and for catching drafts the official feeds bury, but secondary — always resolve back to the eKLEP/PSP primary document.

source_name: Kurzy.cz — mirrored MF/agency legislative press notices
why_relevant: Aggregator that republishes MF comment-procedure notices verbatim; useful as a redundancy channel and as an RSS-friendly proxy if mf.gov.cz crawling becomes unreliable.

source_name: Financnigramotnost.gov.cz — MF financial-literacy portal legislative notices
why_relevant: MF-operated satellite site that mirrors consumer-facing financial legislation notices (e.g. consumer credit amendment comment procedure); occasionally posts items with different phrasing/timing than the main MF site.

source_name: Vláda ČR — Legislativní pravidla vlády / metodika zpracování materiálů
why_relevant: Defines the mandatory structure of a Czech bill package (návrh zákona, důvodová zpráva, RIA, srovnávací tabulky, seznam připomínkových míst) and the standard comment period. Essential to build reliable extraction rules and to know what documents must exist for any MF bill.
